clue.text: During return visit one planted a small tree

indicators.note: planted says one piece is set down into the middle of another
return asks for the word for a visit to be read backwards

parts.note: to visit is to call on someone
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone pays a second visit and plants a little tree while there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns CALL into LLAC, and 'planted' sets I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The lilac is a shrub or small tree with fragrant purple or white flowers.

clue.text: Time for feast of meat, mostly, with fruit and fish

indicators.note: mostly says the word loses its final letter

parts.note: lamb is a meat
mast is the fallen fruit of beech and oak trees
the ide is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A festival season with a meal of meat, fruit and fish.
explanation.walkthrough: MAST is the nuts of forest trees; the IDE is a European carp-like fish.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the old English harvest festival season around 1 August, when loaves from the first wheat were blessed.

clue.text: Not professionally qualified to prepare for a meal

definitions.meaning: to set a table with cutlery and plates

explanation.definitionFit: An amateur is a layman, and setting out plates and cutlery is to set the table.

clue.text: A post dodged by shirkers

definitions.meaning: a ...-dodger is old military slang for someone who avoids duty

explanation.definitionFit: A pillar is an upright support, and shirkers who avoid duty are called column-dodgers.

clue.text: Stacks of fruit identified in comic verses.

parts.note: a lime is a citrus fruit
ricks are stacks of hay or straw

explanation.surface: Piles of fruit turn up in some funny poems.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue lists the pieces in the opposite order to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Five-line humorous poems with an AABBA rhyme are the classic form of light comic verse.

clue.text: HGV charge included in this sort of case

indicators.note: included in places one piece within another

parts.note: the clue's words after HGV are printed in lower case
a charge is a load, as one carried

explanation.surface: A lorry charge is covered in some kind of container.
explanation.walkthrough: HGV is a heavy goods vehicle, a British term for a big lorry; 'this sort of case' means the small letters the rest of the clue is printed in.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy goods vehicle with a low flat trailer for carrying machinery is a type of lorry.

clue.text: Female graduate's upset appearance

parts.note: MA is a Master of Arts

indicators.note: upset in a down clue turns the word over, reading it upwards

parts.note: an air is an appearance or manner

explanation.surface: A woman with a degree looks troubled.
explanation.definitionFit: A common woman's given name stands for a female in general.

clue.text: Pragmatic people are distraught over scene of combat

indicators.note: over in a down clue places one piece above another
distraught suggests the little word is thrown into disorder

parts.note: the lists were the enclosed ground for jousting

explanation.surface: Practical folk are upset by a battlefield.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who face facts and act practically are pragmatists, people with a down-to-earth outlook.

clue.text: Positive contribution, at first, in relating to class

indicators.note: in places the opening letter inside another word

parts.note: categorial means relating to categories or classes

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of contribution

explanation.surface: Being certain about one's input when it comes to social class.
explanation.definitionFit: Being absolutely certain and unqualified is to be emphatic, without any doubt.

clue.text: Time to abandon barren island

indicators.note: to abandon says one letter leaves the word

parts.note: stark means bare or barren

explanation.surface: It is time to leave a bleak isle.
explanation.walkthrough: Sark is one of the Channel Islands.
explanation.definitionFit: This small isle is one of the Channel Islands, between England and France.

clue.text: From 2 we reconstructed a famous vessel

indicators.note: reconstructed says the letters gathered here are rebuilt in a new order

parts.note: the answer to 2 Down, meaning not professionally qualified

explanation.surface: Starting from a clue elsewhere, we rebuild a celebrated ship.
explanation.walkthrough: '2' points to the answer of 2 Down, LAY; with FROM and WE it gives the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: The ship that carried the Pilgrim Fathers to America in 1620 is one of history's best-known vessels.

clue.text: Introduce new variation, say, in place of sacrifice

indicators.note: say tells us the word is spoken, so a word that sounds the same is entered

parts.note: to introduce a new variation is to alter something

explanation.surface: A suggestion to make changes at the site of an offering.
explanation.definitionFit: In a church or temple the raised table where offerings were made is the site of sacrifice.

clue.text: Ready to do a good turn providing quarters

definitions.text: Ready to do a good turn

definitions.meaning: offering lodging or rooms to stay in

explanation.definitionFit: Obliging people go out of their way for others, and a building that houses guests offers them lodging.

clue.text: Puzzles involving son in clash

indicators.note: involving says one piece wraps around another

parts.note: grid word puzzles like this one

explanation.surface: A boy gets caught up in a quarrel over puzzles.
explanation.definitionFit: To clash or fight with someone is the idiom of fencers crossing blades.

clue.text: Bishop seen with sexy photo? That takes the biscuit!

parts.note: B abbreviates bishop in chess
randy means sexually eager
a snap is a snapshot

explanation.surface: A clergyman photographed in a racy picture is outrageous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That takes the biscuit!' is a British exclamation meaning that is the limit.
explanation.definitionFit: This thin, crisp, rolled ginger confection is a kind of sweet biscuit.

clue.text: Hardy sergeant captured by the Greeks

definitions.meaning: Sergeant Frank ... is the dashing soldier in Thomas Hardy's novel Far from the Madding Crowd
the city taken by the Greeks with the wooden horse

explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Hardy was an English novelist; his sergeant shares his name with the city of the Trojan War.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share the name: Hardy's soldier character and the ancient city sacked in the Trojan War.

clue.text: Soldier of fortune coming to confluence of two rivers

parts.note: an advent is a coming or arrival
the Ure is a Yorkshire river
R is the usual abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A mercenary arrives where two streams meet.
explanation.walkthrough: The URE is a river in Yorkshire; 'confluence of' just joins the two rivers side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A mercenary or fortune-seeker who takes risks for gain is a classic adventurer.

clue.text: One who improves parts of Notre Dame

indicators.note: parts of suggests the name broken up and its pieces rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone restores sections of the Paris cathedral.
explanation.definitionFit: An editor who corrects a text is a corrector, one who makes it better.

clue.text: English king songwriter first presented as German

indicators.note: first says this piece comes before the others

parts.note: Irving Berlin, the American songwriter
R, for rex, is king

explanation.surface: An English king and a songwriter are introduced as German.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of the German capital is a citizen of the country's largest city.

clue.text: Cast down when food consumed, chokes king

parts.note: a dish is a serving of food

indicators.note: chokes suggests one piece gripping another round its middle

parts.note: consumed means eaten
R, for Latin rex, abbreviates king

explanation.surface: After a meal, the monarch chokes and someone is cast down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chokes' puts R inside EATEN to give EARTEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To cast someone down is to depress or demoralise them, robbing them of courage.

clue.text: Religious work found in attic once

indicators.note: found in says the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A sacred painting turns up in the loft one day.
explanation.definitionFit: An Orthodox devotional painting of a saint on wood is a religious artwork.

clue.text: Is military leader able to go up for a drink?

indicators.note: to go up in a down clue turns each word upwards

parts.note: GOC is General Officer Commanding
can means able to

explanation.surface: Can the general manage to go to the bar?
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go up' turns GOC into COG and CAN into NAC in place.
explanation.definitionFit: A brandy distilled in western France is a spirit, an alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: Unrefined Irish writer joining English archaeologist, say

indicators.note: say means the name pair is heard rather than read

parts.note: Oscar Wilde, joined by 'and' to Sir Leonard Woolley, excavator of Ur

explanation.surface: An Irish author teams up with an English digger.
explanation.walkthrough: Leonard Woolley was the English archaeologist who excavated Ur; 'Wilde and Woolley' spoken sounds like the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough, uncouth or lawless character is described with this idiom, untamed and lacking polish.

clue.text: Friendship is just what's needed in a cruising vessel

definitions.text: Friendship is just what's needed in a cruising vessel

parts.words: Friendship is just what's needed in a cruising vessel
parts.note: reads as advice on getting along at sea, but asks for a word for goodwill, as if it were itself a ship's name

explanation.definitionFit: Goodwill and harmony between people is friendship.

clue.text: Lincoln died thus? Yes, in fact

definitions.text: Lincoln died thus? Yes, in fact

parts.note: Abe is Abraham Lincoln's nickname

explanation.surface: A question about how the president met his end.
explanation.walkthrough: Lincoln was shot at a theatre but died in a bed in a house across the street.
explanation.definitionFit: In bed is how Lincoln died, at the Petersen House.

clue.text: Powerful businessman's cut

definitions.meaning: a tycoon or magnate in some industry
a ... of beef is a joint made of two sirloins

explanation.definitionFit: A press magnate is called by the old noble title, which also names a large joint of beef or lamb.

clue.text: Point where campers may be immediately after crossing island

parts.note: campers may be in a tent
on can mean immediately after, as in 'on arrival'

explanation.surface: Campers settle down straight after getting across to an island.
explanation.definitionFit: The point of doing something is its aim or purpose.

clue.text: Diamonds made of carbon — that's about it

indicators.note: about says one piece goes around another

parts.note: i.e. is Latin id est, that is
C is the chemical symbol for carbon

explanation.surface: Diamonds are only carbon, and that is all there is to it.
explanation.definitionFit: In criminal slang gems and jewels are called by the word for frozen water.

clue.text: Stupidly steer dory into ship

indicators.note: stupidly says the letters that follow are put together in a foolish new order

explanation.surface: Someone clumsily steers a small boat into a larger ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A fast naval warship that escorts fleets is a type of ship.

clue.text: How birds may be said to go for a song

indicators.note: may be said signals that a word spoken aloud gives the entry

parts.note: birds go cheep, the sound of a chick

explanation.surface: A remark on the noise birds make when they sing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go' joins the bird noise to its sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Bought for a song means bought for very little money, at a low price.
